matches.title: Telegram number has a leading zero
matches.anti_pattern: Leading zeros creep into telegram numbers.
matches.approved_practice: Strip leading zeros from telegram numbers unless the source image proves the zero is part of a non-telegram identifier.
matches.comment_text: Check whether this telegram number has an unintended leading zero. FRUS style should not preserve compiler-added leading zeros in telegram numbers.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Telegram sourced from WHSR/NSC copy without eRecords/drafting check
matches.matched_text: White House Situation Room copy of outgoing Nodis telegram
matches.anti_pattern: Relying on White House Situation Room or NSC copies of telegrams, especially outgoing Nodis telegrams, without going back to eRecords for the Department of State copy and drafting information.
matches.approved_practice: Use eRecords/Department of State telegram copies when available; when WHSR or NSC copies are genuinely needed, capture outgoing drafting, clearance, approval, and header data from eRecords if possible.
matches.comment_text: Confirm whether an eRecords/Department of State telegram copy exists and whether outgoing drafting information has been captured before finalizing this source note.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Cross-reference slug or clue is incomplete
matches.anti_pattern: Cross-reference clues lack date, sender/recipient, document type, and an above/below/chapter indicator.
matches.approved_practice: Before final review, complete intra-volume and inter-volume slugs with date, sender/recipient, type, and above/below/chapter indicator, all struck through if they remain compiler-facing clues.
matches.comment_text: Complete the cross-reference clue with date, sender/recipient, document type, and above/below/chapter indicator before final style review.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Page break may be missing between document annotations
matches.anti_pattern: Annotations for separate documents run together because page breaks were not inserted.
matches.approved_practice: Insert a page break between document annotations before handoff unless the production template explicitly manages document boundaries.
matches.comment_text: Check document boundary formatting and insert the missing page break before editor handoff.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: First footnote remains attached to document heading
matches.anti_pattern: The first footnote sits on the document heading although current practice no longer requires it.
matches.approved_practice: Do not retain the first footnote on the document heading merely because that used to be standard; place source-note apparatus where current FRUS practice requires.
matches.comment_text: Check whether the first footnote is still attached to the document heading under an older practice and should be moved.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Word auto-numbering or auto-formatting may have shaped footnotes
matches.anti_pattern: Auto-numbering and auto-formatting remain enabled and can corrupt or obscure FRUS footnote form.
matches.approved_practice: Turn off Word auto-numbering/auto-formatting for production footnotes and manually verify numbering/formatting before handoff.
matches.comment_text: Verify that Word auto-numbering/auto-formatting has not controlled FRUS footnote form.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Document may be incomplete or missing pages
matches.anti_pattern: Incomplete documents are turned in, sometimes with pages missing outright.
matches.approved_practice: Confirm page completeness against the source image, scan, or backup before final style review.
matches.comment_text: Verify document completeness and recover missing pages before finalizing the annotation sheet.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Source note still contains compiler shorthand
matches.anti_pattern: Source notes remain incomplete or carry compiler shorthand.
matches.approved_practice: Expand shorthand into final FRUS source-note form before redline handoff; unresolved shorthand belongs in comments or the evidence queue, not publishable apparatus.
matches.comment_text: Expand compiler shorthand into final source-note form or move the unresolved item to an evidence-request comment.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Quoted material in backup may not be highlighted
matches.anti_pattern: Quoted material in backup documents is not highlighted for editors.
matches.approved_practice: Highlight quoted material in backup documents so editors can verify quotations quickly.
matches.comment_text: Confirm the backup document highlights all quoted material used in the annotation sheet.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Backup telegram copy may omit header or film/reel numbers
matches.anti_pattern: Backup telegram copies omit header information, including film number, preventing editors from verifying D, P, and N reel numbers.
matches.approved_practice: Print backup telegram headers, including film number and D/P/N reel data, so editors can verify the communications metadata.
matches.comment_text: Verify that the backup telegram copy includes the full header, film number, and D/P/N reel information.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Style Guide adherence is inconsistent
matches.anti_pattern: The sheet is inconsistent about adhering to the FRUS Style Guide.
matches.approved_practice: Use the checker as a bespoke spellcheck pass for Style Guide consistency; tally recurring unresolved variants separately for General Editor decision.
matches.comment_text: Run a final Style Guide consistency pass and move unresolved recurring variants to the General Editor discrepancy tally.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession generalized for all compiler sheets.

matches.title: Document XX cross-reference construction is incomplete or malformed
matches.anti_pattern: Using Document XX, Doc. XX, Document TK/TBD, or a bare/malformed internal Document reference in annotation-sheet clues.
matches.approved_practice: For published internal references, follow Reagan Foundations forms such as `See Document 69.`, `Printed as Document 155.`, `see footnote 9, Document 56`, and `See Document 34 and footnote 2 thereto.` For compiler-facing annotation-sheet clues, finish the struck-through bracketed clue with date, sender/recipient, document type, and above/below/chapter indicator before handoff.
matches.comment_text: Check this Document cross-reference construction against the target volume. If it remains a compiler-facing clue, complete the date, sender/recipient, document type, and above/below/chapter locator; if it is final apparatus, use the published FRUS form.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson recurring-risk confession and follow-up note; Reagan Foundations published examples: Documents 45, 74, 161, and 316.

matches.title: Footnote refer-back rule may be missed after repeated references
matches.anti_pattern: Repeating full citation/source details after the threshold for a refer-back has been reached, or using a bare see-footnote construction without Document or above/below context.
matches.approved_practice: After repeated references to the same item, refer back rather than reciting the citation again: within the same document use `see footnote 5, above` or a bare same-document parenthetical only when the sentence itself supplies the above/below context; across documents use `see footnote 9, Document 56`, `see footnote 6, Document 265 and footnote 2, Document 312`, or `See Document 34 and footnote 2 thereto`; straight document references use `See Document 69.` Treat the three-times threshold as a production-review trigger requiring human confirmation of the target.
matches.comment_text: Check whether this repeated reference should use a footnote refer-back. Reagan Foundations models same-document `see footnote N, above`, same-document local-context `B above (see footnote N)`, and cross-document `see footnote N, Document X` forms; confirm the target before rewriting.
matches.source_basis: James Wilson follow-up note on the footnote refer-back rule; Reagan Foundations published examples: Documents 45, 74, 146, 217, 267, and 316.
